subject: Alphanumeric literals
notes: cite.py --check 8.3.3.2.4 "If character-1 is not specified, the literal is a zero-length literal" OK. Zero-length: IsZeroLength asks the structural question (Body.Length==2) for "" and ''; probe p1 MOVE ""/'' TO W gives spaces (the 14.9.25.4 GR2 substitution, pinned by pb425). a)/b) compile-time value -> runtime value: the project's alphanumeric repertoire is UTF-16 (charset decision), so the compile-time string IS the runtime string; probe p11/p12: VALUE "\u00e9\u4e2dZ" displays e-acute,CJK,Z (UTF-8 bytes c3 a9 e4 b8 ad 5a at the display boundary), LENGTH("\u00e9\u4e2d")=2, ORD("\u00e9")=234. c) is conditional on the implementor PROVIDING a UTF-8 / mixed option; none is provided (no such option in the CLI or OPTIONS paragraph), so c) imposes nothing -- the Annex A item 38 documentation row is a separate DOC rule. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2014, 2023 (Annex E itemizes the 2014->2023 delta and lists no change to 8.3.3.2, so the rule stands in both; the 1985/2002 edge is NOT derivable in-repo -- no 2002 or 1985 text is held) retired-witness: conformance:2002/pb425_zero_length_literal_move (the golden moved to the 2014 corpus: it writes a zero-length literal, a COBOL-2014 introduction gated by kb/Work PB895 (same program, same expected output))
